about.disclaimer_body: OSRS Events is a fan-made project and is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to Jagex Ltd. Old School RuneScape is a trademark of Jagex Ltd.
about.feature_boards_desc: Run a Snakes & Ladders board with an OSRS task on every tile, or a skill race scored straight off the hiscores.
about.feature_dark_desc: Easy on the eyes whether you grind at noon or 2 AM. Dark mode is always available.
about.feature_dice_desc: On a board, roll a d6 each day and advance. Roll limits keep it competitive without turning it into a grind.
about.feature_discord_desc: Log in with Discord, or with an email address if you prefer. Either way your progress is saved automatically.
about.feature_free_desc: No premium tiers, no paywalls. Everything is free. If you enjoy it, consider a donation!
about.feature_tasks_desc: Every board tile has an OSRS task. Complete it in-game and mark it done to unlock your next roll.
about.free_body: This project is run by a player, for players. Hosting and maintenance cost real money, so if you find value in the platform, a small donation helps keep the lights on.
about.privacy_body: We collect the minimum needed to run the platform — your Discord username, ID and avatar if you log in that way, or your email address if you sign up directly, plus the OSRS account name used to score you in events. We do not track you, show you ads, or sell your data to anyone. Full details are in our Privacy Policy.
about.subtitle: An OSRS-themed events platform for clans, made with love for the community.
about.support_body: Have a question, found a bug, or want to suggest a feature? Send me an email and I'll get back to you as soon as I can.
about.title: About

landing.clan_events.faq_a4: The board stays available to read after its end date, so you keep the final standings and can look back at previous events.

landing.clan_events.feature_boards_desc: Build a 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9 board and put an OSRS task on every tile, pulled straight from the OSRS Wiki.
landing.clan_events.feature_discord_desc: Lock a board to your clan's Discord server so only members can join. No whitelist to maintain by hand.
landing.clan_events.feature_free_desc: No paid tier, no ads and no player cap. Donations cover hosting.
landing.clan_events.feature_invites_desc: Generate invite links with expiry dates and use limits, and revoke any of them at any time.
landing.clan_events.feature_leaderboard_: Every board has a leaderboard, so the clan can see where everyone stands without asking in chat.
landing.clan_events.feature_teams_desc: Split the roster into teams that share one board position, or let everyone play their own board solo.
landing.clan_events.lead: Everything you need to run an Old School RuneScape clan event: board building, Discord-based access, teams and live progress tracking. Free, with no ads.
landing.clan_events.meta_desc: Run Old School RuneScape clan events for free. Build task boards, group members into teams from your Discord server and track everyone's progress in one place.
landing.clan_events.meta_title: OSRS Clan Events — Free Event Board Platform
landing.clan_events.setup_body: Start smaller than you think you should. A 5×5 board over a weekend tells you how your clan actually engages, and costs an afternoon to build. Set a daily roll limit so the event paces itself rather than being finished by Sunday. Write your tasks to be checkable from a screenshot — 'get a Dragon Warhammer' settles cleanly, 'do some slayer' does not. Then post the board link in your Discord and pin it, because the single most common reason a clan event dies is that half the roster never found the link.
landing.clan_events.title: OSRS Clan Events
landing.clan_events.what_subtitle: The parts of running an event that usually eat an organiser's week.
landing.clan_events.why_body: A clan is at its healthiest when members log in with a reason to. Events give the roster a shared goal, pull semi-inactive members back, and give newer players a way to contribute that does not depend on gear or kill count. The idea was never the hard part — the tracking was. Most clans end up with a spreadsheet nobody updates and a Discord thread of screenshots nobody reads.
landing.event_ideas.idea1_desc: Every tile is an OSRS task and players roll a daily d6 to advance. Ladders jump you forward, snakes drop you back. Because a dice roll sits between a player and their next task, hours played matter less than in any other format here — a casual member can genuinely beat a maxed main, which keeps the event competitive to the final day.
landing.event_ideas.idea2_desc: A grid of drop or achievement tiles; teams race to complete rows, columns or the full board. Far and away the most popular OSRS event format, and the most demanding. It rewards raw hours, so a few grinders usually decide it early unless you weight the tiles carefully.
landing.event_ideas.idea3_desc: Pick a boss list and a point value per unique, then let teams log drops for a fixed window. Short, trivial to explain and almost setup-free — but it heavily favours whoever can commit the whole weekend.
landing.event_ideas.idea4_desc: Everyone starts from their current XP in a chosen skill and races for the biggest gain. Fair by construction, because it measures change rather than total: a level 60 and a level 99 compete on equal terms.
landing.event_ideas.idea5_desc: Post a fixed set of encounters and let members submit times. It runs indefinitely with no end date, which makes it the lowest-maintenance option on this list — good as a permanent background event between bigger ones.
landing.event_ideas.idea6_desc: Points for diary tiers or quests completed inside the event window. One of the few formats where newer accounts have the advantage, since veterans have already finished everything. Excellent for onboarding a wave of new members.
landing.event_ideas.idea7_desc: Each team hides ships on a grid and fires by completing tasks. Very social and very chat-heavy, but it needs an organiser watching it daily — the format lives or dies on somebody refereeing it.
landing.event_ideas.idea8_desc: Track collection log slots filled across the whole clan against one shared target. Cooperative rather than competitive, which suits clans where a leaderboard would put people off rather than draw them in.
landing.event_ideas.idea8_meta: Long-term clans · a month or more
landing.event_ideas.intro: The best clan event is the one your members finish. A format that carries a 200-member PvM clan will die quietly in a 15-person social clan, and the reverse is just as true. Below is what each format actually rewards, so you can choose on purpose instead of copying whatever the last clan did.
landing.event_ideas.lead: Eight event formats OSRS clans actually run, what each one rewards, and how to pick the one that fits your roster.
landing.event_ideas.meta_desc: Eight Old School RuneScape clan event ideas compared: what each format rewards, how long to run it, and which clan sizes it actually suits.
landing.event_ideas.meta_title: OSRS Clan Event Ideas — 8 Formats Compared
landing.event_ideas.pick_body: Two questions settle it. First: how much time does your median member have — not your most active one? Formats that reward raw hours reward the top ten percent of your roster and quietly tell everybody else not to bother. Second: who is going to run it? Every format above needs somebody approving completions and answering questions daily. If nobody has volunteered for that yet, run a shorter event than the one you want.
landing.event_ideas.supported_body: OSRS Events currently runs Snakes & Ladders boards with OSRS Wiki task integration, Discord-based access control, teams and live leaderboards. Bingo boards are the next event type on the roadmap.
landing.event_ideas.title: OSRS Clan Event Ideas

landing.snakes.how_title: How an OSRS Snakes & Ladders event works
landing.snakes.lead: A free Snakes & Ladders board built for Old School RuneScape clans. Every tile is an OSRS task — complete it to keep climbing, or hit a snake and slide back down.
landing.snakes.meta_desc: Build a free Old School RuneScape Snakes & Ladders board for your clan. Assign OSRS tasks to every tile, roll a daily d6 and track everyone's progress.
landing.snakes.meta_title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders — Free Board Generator
landing.snakes.modes_body: Solo boards give every player their own position and their own daily roll. Team boards give each team one shared position, so the team decides together which task to take on next. Teams can be tied to your Discord server so members are grouped automatically instead of by hand.
landing.snakes.size_5_desc: A weekend event. A good first run, and enough for a smaller clan.
landing.snakes.size_7_desc: The usual pick. Comfortably fills one to two weeks of play.
landing.snakes.size_9_desc: A month-long clan event, with room for genuine long-grind tasks.
landing.snakes.sizes_subtitle: Pick the size from how long you want the event to run, not from how big your clan is.
landing.snakes.step1_desc: Pick 5×5, 7×7 or 9×9, name the event, and set the start and end dates.
landing.snakes.step2_desc: Every tile gets an Old School RuneScape task. Search the OSRS Wiki from inside the tile editor and the icon and title fill themselves in.
landing.snakes.step3_desc: Choose which tiles launch a player up the board and which drop them back down. No two boards play the same.
landing.snakes.step4_desc: Open the board to anyone, lock it to your Discord server, or hand out invite links you can revoke.
landing.snakes.step5_desc: Players roll a d6 each day, complete the task they land on and mark the tile off. First to the final tile wins.
landing.snakes.title: OSRS Snakes & Ladders
landing.snakes.why_body: Bingo rewards whoever grinds the most hours, so the clan's biggest account usually settles it in the first weekend and everyone else stops paying attention. Snakes & Ladders puts a dice roll between a player and their next task. That single change means a casual member can climb past a maxed main, and the event stays live to the final day instead of being decided early.
landing.snakes.why_title: Why Snakes & Ladders instead of bingo?

privacy.data_discord_id_desc: Your unique Discord identifier. Used to link your account across sessions and to identify you within the game.
privacy.data_intro: When you log in with Discord, we receive the following information from Discord's OAuth2 API:
privacy.data_nickname_desc: A custom display name you may set yourself in your profile. Replaces your Discord username wherever your name appears.
privacy.data_progress_desc: Your current tile position, completed tiles, and daily dice roll count on each board you participate in.
privacy.data_username_desc: Your Discord username at the time of login. Displayed on your profile and to other players on shared boards.
privacy.discord_note: Discord is used solely for authentication. Once logged in, we do not send any further data to Discord. Discord may log the OAuth2 authorisation request on their end.
privacy.intro_body: OSRS Events ("the Service") is a fan-made web application. We are committed to protecting your privacy and being transparent about what little data we store. This page explains what information is collected when you use the Service, how it is used, and your rights.
privacy.no_analytics: Analytics, page views, or behavioural tracking
privacy.no_collect_body: We intentionally collect as little as possible. The following data is never collected:
privacy.no_sell: Any data sold or shared with third parties for commercial purposes
privacy.rights_body: You have the right to access, correct, or delete the data we hold about you at any time. Logging out removes your local session token. To request permanent deletion of your account and all associated data, please contact us.
privacy.rights_contact_body: Send us an email with the subject 'Account deletion request' and we will remove your account and all associated data within a reasonable timeframe.
privacy.storage_body: Your data is stored in a private PostgreSQL database. A JSON Web Token (JWT) is saved in your browser's localStorage to keep you logged in for up to 7 days. This token contains only your user ID and is never shared with third parties. You can clear it at any time by logging out.
privacy.subtitle: We believe your data is yours. Here is exactly what we collect and why.
privacy.third_party_body: We use one external service as part of the login flow:
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

profile.osrs_account_help: Your Old School RuneScape account name. Used to look up XP gains for skill races — nothing else reads it.
profile.password_needs_email: Add an email address first — without one you could never reset this password.
profile.title: Profile
seo.about_desc: OSRS Events is a free, ad-free platform for running Old School RuneScape clan events — Snakes & Ladders boards and skill races, with Discord login and OSRS Wiki task integration.
seo.board_desc: Play the :title Old School RuneScape event board on OSRS Events. Roll your daily dice, complete OSRS tasks and climb the leaderboard.
seo.boards_desc: Browse public Old School RuneScape clan events. Join an open Snakes & Ladders board or a skill race and start competing with your clan.
seo.home_desc: Run free Old School RuneScape clan events. Build a Snakes & Ladders board with OSRS tasks on every tile, or race on skill XP with a live leaderboard.
seo.home_title: OSRS Events — Free Snakes & Ladders and Skill Races for Clans
seo.leaderboard_desc: Live standings for the :title Old School RuneScape event board. See which players and teams are furthest along.
seo.privacy_desc: How OSRS Events handles your data: what is stored from Discord login, what is never collected, and how to have your account removed.
seo.teams_desc: Manage the teams taking part in your Old School RuneScape clan events, grouped by Discord server.
seo.terms_desc: The terms for using OSRS Events, a free fan-made Old School RuneScape clan event platform that is not affiliated with Jagex.

terms.account_rule_one: You will only maintain one account per person.
terms.accounts_body: To use the Service you must authenticate via a valid Discord account. By doing so you agree that:
